story.title: Iran Sets Conditions for Reopening the Strait of Hormuz
story.summary: Iran has stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until seven specific conditions, outlined in a June interim agreement with the US, are fulfilled. This announcement was made by Iran's parliament speaker during the UN General Assembly, where a proposal was also presented to potentially reopen the strait within seven days if the conditions are met.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Discusses Iran Decision at UN, Threatens Annihilation or Deal
timeline_highlights.summary: During his speech at the United Nations General Assembly, President Trump stated he faces a significant decision regarding Iran: to either negotiate a deal or consider military action, which he described as the potential to 'annihilate' the regime. He expressed confidence that Tehran might seek a resolution after the upcoming US midterm elections, emphasizing the importance of preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

He mentioned the possibility of annihilating Iran if no deal is reached.
Trump predicted that Iran would seek a deal after the US midterm elections.

timeline_highlights.title: Iran Proposes Seven-Day Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz Amid US Discussions
timeline_highlights.summary: Iran has proposed a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, contingent on meeting certain conditions. The Iranian Foreign Minister stated that normal maritime traffic could resume if these conditions are satisfied. Meanwhile, a US official indicated that constructive discussions are ongoing through mediators, although President Trump has reportedly rejected the Iranian proposal.

related_stories.title: Bosnia Holds Elections Amid Ethnic Tensions and Pro-Russian Political Influence
related_stories.summary: Bosnia is conducting elections where approximately 3.4 million voters are selecting members for the multi-ethnic presidency, national Parliament lawmakers, and heads of institutions for the country's two entities. The elections are marked by the significant presence of a pro-Russian politician and ongoing ethnic tensions, alongside concerns regarding the stalled European Union membership bid.

related_stories.title: Cornell President Responds to Alleged Gang Rape Incident at Fraternity
related_stories.summary: Cornell University's president, Michael Kotlikoff, described the allegations of a gang rape involving a student at a fraternity house as 'deeply disturbing.' In a recent video statement, he emphasized the need for the university to improve its response to such incidents. The allegations have led to increased scrutiny of the university's handling of sexual assault cases, with the accuser, identified as Jane Doe, suing the university and several former students.

related_stories.title: Brazilians Begin Voting in Polarized Presidential Election
related_stories.summary: Voting has commenced in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, featuring incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election is marked by a deeply polarized atmosphere, with polls indicating a tight race that may lead to a runoff. Approximately 160 million voters are also selecting lawmakers, senators, and governors in this significant electoral event.

related_stories.title: Trump Calls for Action Against Senator Cotton Over Daylight Saving Bill
related_stories.summary: Trump has urged the public to contact Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas, accusing him of obstructing a bill aimed at making daylight saving time permanent. In a controversial move, Trump also shared Cotton's cell phone number to encourage constituents to voice their concerns directly.
